parity_risks.note: The Input tool's own query carries `WHERE AMOUNT <> 0`. The procedure reads the mapped table rather than running that query, so the predicate has to be written out again in t1_input; without it every zero or NULL amount would reach the segment, which Alteryx never saw.

Filter [REGION] = [User.Region]: a NULL REGION makes the expression NULL, and Alteryx sends both false AND NULL to the False anchor. That anchor is not wired, so those rows simply leave the workflow -- which is also what a three-valued SQL WHERE does with them.

[User.Region] is a workflow constant, not a column. Its value ('EMEA') is resolved at translation time into a literal; nothing at run time supplies it, and a run wanting another region needs a new procedure.

The DateTime tool reads dd/mm/yyyy text and writes NULL for text the format cannot read, so TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ (not TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ) is the warn-and-null form; 31/02/2026 is the row that proves it.
POSTED_DT is an Alteryx DateTime, so a parsed date carries midnight: the column is TIMESTAMP_NTZ, not DATE, and comparing it against a DATE would be a type difference.
